occupation.note: 'Nelson R. Norton, ship-carpenter, and builder of the first draw-bridge over the main river, at Dearborn Street, in March, 1834, came November 16, 1833 (he also built the first sloop, the "Clarissa," launched May 12, 1836)'.

persons.note: AN ARRIVAL DATED TO THE DAY - 16 NOVEMBER 1833 - which only four households in this parcel have, and a trade that ties a person to two dated artefacts. HE IS IN THE DATASET BECAUSE THE 1835 TOWN CANNOT BE BUILT WITHOUT HIS TRADE. Andreas's roster is the only list this project holds that names artisans at all, and every name on it is a documented alternative to an inferred one.

resident_research.evidence_for: Early Chicago history preserves Nelson R. Norton's own chronology: arrival November 16, 1833, construction of the Dearborn Street drawbridge beginning March 1834 and completion around June. Exact name plus the distinctive shipwright/bridge role corroborate the person.

research_note: THE ONLY SHIPWRIGHT IN THE DATASET, in a town whose whole future was a harbour. He is also the parcel's clearest example of a trade the structures layer already depends on: data/structures/dearborn_street_drawbridge.json models a bridge whose builder now has a name, an arrival date and a second, later vessel to his credit.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
